incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: service=redwood-web-frontend alert=alb-target-unhealthy severity=page — link=<pd://INCIDENT/12345>

pagerduty-bot: Paging oncall: John (oncall) — Incident ID 2026-03-14-ALB-01

John (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. First glance: ALB target-group showing ~40% unhealthy in ap-northeast-1. Users reporting TLS handshake failures.

Maria (sre): Pulling ALB access logs + target health. Seeing `SSL handshake failure` entries with `alert unknown ca` from the ALB -> targets path.

Sam (eng-prod): We ran the cert rotation pipeline ~5m before the page. Possible intermediate cert was not uploaded to a subset of proxies.

Katie (netops): DNS check: global propagation is uneven — some edge nodes still resolving old ELB IPs. TTL was 300s but updates look mixed. Could explain region skew.

John (oncall): Plan: 1) Rollback cert to last-known-good on proxies 2) Force ALB target re-registration / health-check 3) If TLS not restored quickly consider temporary TCP passthrough listener to bypass proxy (last resort).

pagerduty-bot: Escalating to SRE lead after 5m no full recovery — Maria notified.

Maria (sre): Starting rollback. Sam — please push `cert-2026-03-12.pem` to proxy ASG with emergency tag.

Sam (eng-prod): Kicking rollback job now: `./deploy_cert.sh --target proxy-asg --cert cert-2026-03-12.pem --tag emergency`

incident-bot: Deploy job started — rolling update 3/12 proxies (job id: deploy-6789).

Katie (netops): While that runs, I'm lowering Route53 failover TTL to 60s and shifting health checks to prefer us-west-2 for external CNAMEs to reduce EU impact.

Ryan (support): Support reports: ~8% of traffic erroring with TLS failures, mostly EU users. No top-tier customers reported full outage yet but multiple tickets opened.

Emily (customer-sa): Notified top 5 EU customers proactively. They want ETA and mitigation steps.

Sam (eng-prod): Rollback completed on 3/12 proxies. Triggering ALB target re-evaluation.

Sam (eng-prod): ALB target health snippet:
```text
target 10.0.12.34:443 -> Unhealthy (502)
target 10.0.12.35:443 -> Healthy
target 10.0.12.36:443 -> Healthy
...
```

John (oncall): Observability shows request success rate climbing to ~98% in ap-northeast-1. EU still has some residual TLS errors — likely DNS caches/edges resolving to older endpoints.

Maria (sre): Confirming — TLS handshake errors dropped sharply post-rollback. ALB logs returning normal. Continuing to monitor for 60m.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PagerDuty incident acknowledged and updated — responders: John (oncall), Maria (sre), Sam (eng-prod).

John (oncall): Handoff: Maria will own live monitoring and post-incident writeup. I'll stay on standby for 30m, then hand off fully.

Maria (sre): Taking ownership for next 90 minutes. Action items: 1) Validate health in all regions 2) Update cert rotation automation to ensure full chain uploaded 3) Draft RCA and timeline.

Sam (eng-prod): Root cause hypothesis: cert rotation job missed uploading intermediate CA on a subset of proxy instances due to a packaging bug in our `cert-manager` wrapper. Will open a bug and a hotfix PR.

Emily (customer-sa): Sent customer update: we identified a TLS certificate rotation issue affecting a subset of edge proxies; rollback completed; monitoring in place. No escalations so far.

Ryan (support): Marking tickets with workaround: `clear DNS cache / retry` and referencing incident link. Will follow up if any customer reports reopen.

Maria (sre): Timeline notes to include: page fired (1801203456), ack by John, rollback by Sam (deploy-6789), partial DNS propagation lag causing EU-specific errors, recovery observed by 1801205556, monitoring window to 1801207056.

John (oncall): Good work. Postmortem owner: Maria. Target to publish RCA draft by EOD today.

incident-bot: Incident marked for monitoring — auto-close if stable for 30m. Please add any follow-ups to #eng-postmortems.

Maria (sre): Closing thread here; will post the full incident doc + action items once I finish the timeline. Thanks all. :tada:
